claims.text: The baseline alloy is an equimolar Ti-Zr-Hf-Mo-W alloy, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
Arc melting produces a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution of equimolar Ti-Zr-Hf-Mo-W.
Partial replacement of Mo by Re can retain a single-phase high-entropy solid solution in which every constituent is present at no less than 5 at.%.
Arc melting followed by annealing at 1000 °C for 24 hours in an inert atmosphere will homogenize the Re-substituted alloys.
Replacing Mo with Re increases the conduction-electron count.
Replacing Mo with Re increases the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
An increased conduction-electron count elevates the density of states at the Fermi level.
A higher density of states at the Fermi level enhances the electron-phonon coupling constant.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling strengthens Cooper-pair formation.
Stronger electron-phonon coupling raises the superconducting transition temperature.
Increasing Re content will produce both higher Fermi-level density of states and higher superconducting transition temperature than the equimolar Ti-Zr-Hf-Mo-W baseline.
Density of states and superconducting transition temperature will increase systematically together across the Re-substitution series.
The proposed relationship applies only while the alloy remains a single-phase high-entropy solid solution.
Phase segregation or excessive disorder may cause the proposed relationship between Re substitution, density of states, and transition temperature to break down.
Scattering and local inhomogeneity in disordered high-entropy alloys may obscure or modify the density-of-states–transition-temperature relationship.
Low-temperature photoemission spectroscopy, corroborated by calculations, can characterize the relevant Fermi-level density of states.

contradictions.description: Phase segregation is defined as outside the hypothesis's single-phase boundary, yet its observation is also declared to falsify the hypothesis. An out-of-bound sample cannot by itself decisively falsify the mechanism restricted to single-phase alloys.

The intervention requires every element to remain at or above 5 at.%, but the meaning of 10% and 20% Re substitution is not defined. If these are fractions of the original 20 at.% Mo content, Re would be only 2 or 4 at.%; if they are absolute Re contents, 20 at.% Re fully removes Mo rather than partially substituting it.
